title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
statement:
A singly linked list holds `n` values, given in order from head to tail. You are also given a group size `k`.

Split the list into consecutive blocks of exactly `k` nodes, starting from the head. **Reverse the order of the nodes inside every complete block.** If the list ends with fewer than `k` nodes, that last partial block stays exactly as it is.

Only the order of the nodes changes, never the values stored in them. (In an interview you are expected to relink the nodes in place with `O(1)` extra memory; here the list is given as an array of values and you print the final values from head to tail.)

Print the values of the resulting list from head to tail.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers: the values of the list from head to tail.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the values of the list after reversing each complete block of `k` nodes.

examples.explanation: The blocks are [1 2], [3 4] and [5]. The first two are complete and get reversed. The last block has only one node, fewer than k = 2, so it stays.
Blocks [10 20 30] and [40 50 60] are reversed; the trailing [70] has fewer than 3 nodes and is untouched.
k equals n, so the whole list is one complete block and is fully reversed.

complexity.space: O(1) extra with in-place relinking (besides the output)

hints: First reverse a whole linked list with three pointers (previous, current, next). Then reverse only a segment of exactly k nodes.
Before reversing a block, walk k nodes ahead to check that a full block exists. If it does not, leave the rest alone.
Keep a pointer to the tail of the previously processed block. After reversing a block, connect that tail to the block's new head, and the block's new tail becomes the next 'previous tail'.
